items.title: Two partial-summation bounds for the divisor function alpha^{omega(n)}
items.author: Tony Haddad; Dimitris Koukoulopoulos
items.work: On Arratia's coupling and the Dirichlet law for the factors of a random integer
items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the labelled proposition `prel:partial summation bounds` at source lines 1678-1685: two uniform bounds, sum over n <= x of alpha^{omega(n)} << x (log x)^{alpha-1} and sum over x/y < n <= xy of alpha^{omega(n)}/n << (log y)(log(xy))^{alpha-1}, for alpha in [0,1] and x, y >= 2. The author's proof (source lines 1687-1700) splits into two genuinely different regimes: when y >= sqrt(x) the second sum is enlarged to a sum over numbers with all prime factors at most y^3, factored as an Euler product and bounded with 1+t <= e^t along with the strong Mertens estimate (lines 1689-1693); when y <= sqrt(x) the interval is decomposed into dyadic blocks and each block is controlled by the first bound of the proposition, with the count of blocks producing the factor log y (lines 1695-1699). The statement is two inequalities and records neither the Euler product nor the dyadic splitting.

contexts.label: the author's strong Mertens estimate, which the second half of the proof invokes
